info.title: suwagcms
info.description: The suwagcms command: read and change what a bot knows and does in Suwagcms (facts, knowledge bases, articles, procedures, actions, persona), apply changes all or nothing, and create and push versions.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --json
options.description: Print exactly one JSON document on stdout, also when the command fails. [default: False]

options.name: --open
options.description: Open the matching web page instead of printing; a command with no page refuses it. [default: False]

options.name: --server
options.description: The server's address (the web app; the API is under /api). Default: $SUWAGCMS_URL, else suwagcmsUrl in suwagcms/config.yaml under the current folder, else the address saved with `suwagcms server <url>`, else http://localhost:3330.

options.name: --bot
options.description: The bot a command works on. Default: $SUWAGCMS_BOT, else botId in suwagcms/config.yaml under the current folder, else the bot stored with `suwagcms use <id>`.

options.name: --dir
options.description: The folder with config.yaml. Default: suwagcms under the current folder, if it has one.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Say which server address is used and whether the server answers (or --open the web app).

commands.name: server
commands.description: Save the server address that later commands use.

arguments.name: URL
arguments.description: The server's address, e.g. http://localhost:3330

commands.name: bots
commands.description: List the registered bots, register a new one, and ask a bot what it supports.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the registered bots, marking the one you work on with * (or --open the list in the web app).

commands.name: add
commands.description: Register a bot. The CMS never contacts it, so it can be registered before it runs.

options.name: --name
options.description: The name people see.

options.name: --address
options.description: Where the CMS reaches the bot, an absolute http or https address.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The bot's id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. It does not change.

commands.name: declaration
commands.description: Ask the bot what it supports (format version, blocks, actions in its code), keep a good answer with its time and show it (or --open the bot's profile in the web app).

options.name: --stored
options.description: Show the last answer without asking the bot. [default: False]

commands.name: use
commands.description: Store the bot later commands work on, or say which bot is in use.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The bot to store for later commands. Without it, say which bot is in use.

commands.name: facts
commands.description: List, show, add, edit and delete the global facts of a bot.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the global facts of the bot (or --open the Facts screen in the web app).

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show one global fact with its revision (or --open the Facts screen in the web app).

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The fact's name, like customer.city.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add a global fact to the bot.

options.name: --type
options.description: enum, int or text. Changing the type of a fact drops its old constraints.

options.name: --description
options.description: What the fact means; the model reads it.

options.name: --writable-by
options.description: assign, set or correct. Default for a new fact: set.

options.name: --values
options.description: The values of an enum, at least two.

options.name: --min
options.description: The lowest value of an int.

options.name: --max
options.description: The highest value of an int.

options.name: --max-length
options.description: The most characters of a text, above 0.

options.name: --pattern-regex
options.description: The regular expression a whole value of a text must match.

options.name: --pattern-means
options.description: In words, what a value of the pattern looks like.

options.name: --pattern-example
options.description: A value the regex accepts; an empty text removes it.

options.name: --pattern-tell-customer
options.description: upfront or afterRefusal. Default for a new pattern: upfront.

options.name: --no-pattern
options.description: Take the pattern off a text. [default: False]

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The fact's name: camelCase words, which may be joined by dots (customer.city).

commands.name: edit
commands.description: Change a global fact: only the options you give change, the other fields stay.

options.name: --type
options.description: enum, int or text. Changing the type of a fact drops its old constraints.

options.name: --description
options.description: What the fact means; the model reads it.

options.name: --writable-by
options.description: assign, set or correct. Default for a new fact: set.

options.name: --values
options.description: The values of an enum, at least two.

options.name: --min
options.description: The lowest value of an int.

options.name: --max
options.description: The highest value of an int.

options.name: --max-length
options.description: The most characters of a text, above 0.

options.name: --pattern-regex
options.description: The regular expression a whole value of a text must match.

options.name: --pattern-means
options.description: In words, what a value of the pattern looks like.

options.name: --pattern-example
options.description: A value the regex accepts; an empty text removes it.

options.name: --pattern-tell-customer

options.name: --if-revision

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The fact's name, like customer.city. It does not change.

commands.name: delete
commands.description: Delete a global fact. Refused while a procedure uses it, with every place listed; `usage fact <name>` shows them first.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The fact's name, like customer.city.

commands.name: articles
commands.description: List, show, add, edit and delete the articles of a bot.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the articles of the bot, filtered (or --open the Articles screen in the web app, filtered the same).

options.name: --kb
options.description: Only the articles of this knowledge base.

options.name: --language
options.description: Only the articles in this language, which is their knowledge base's: pl or en.

options.name: --text
options.description: Only the articles with this text in the title, id or description, ignoring case. The content is not read.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show one article in full with its revision (or --open the Articles screen in the web app).

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The article's id, like priceList.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add an article to a knowledge base of the bot. Content and guide may come from files, or from stdin with -.

options.name: --kb
options.description: The id of the knowledge base the article is in; changing it moves the article, and the article takes the language of the new base.

options.name: --title
options.description: The article's title.

options.name: --content
options.description: The content: what is true, in Markdown; the customer reads it, through the model, as text. Or use --content-file.

options.name: --content-file
options.description: A file with the content: what is true, in Markdown; the customer reads it, through the model; - reads it from stdin. Or use --content.

options.name: --guide
options.description: The guide: how the model should talk about it, in Markdown; only the model reads it, as text. Or use --guide-file.

options.name: --guide-file
options.description: A file with the guide: how the model should talk about it, in Markdown; only the model reads it; - reads it from stdin. Or use --guide.

options.name: --description
options.description: What the article answers, as plain text; only the bot's search reads it.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The article's id: camelCase, like priceList. It does not change, and is unique across the bot's bases.

commands.name: edit
commands.description: Change an article: only the options you give change, the other fields stay. Its language is its knowledge base's.

options.name: --kb
options.description: The id of the knowledge base the article is in; changing it moves the article, and the article takes the language of the new base.

options.name: --title
options.description: The article's title.

options.name: --content
options.description: The content: what is true, in Markdown; the customer reads it, through the model, as text. Or use --content-file.

options.name: --content-file
options.description: A file with the content: what is true, in Markdown; the customer reads it, through the model; - reads it from stdin. Or use --content.

options.name: --guide
options.description: The guide: how the model should talk about it, in Markdown; only the model reads it, as text. Or use --guide-file.

options.name: --guide-file
options.description: A file with the guide: how the model should talk about it, in Markdown; only the model reads it; - reads it from stdin. Or use --guide.

options.name: --description
options.description: What the article answers, as plain text; only the bot's search reads it.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The article's id: camelCase, like priceList. It does not change, and is unique across the bot's bases.

commands.name: delete
commands.description: Delete an article. Refused while another article links to it, with every referrer listed; `usage article <id>` shows them first.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The article's id, like priceList.

commands.name: kb
commands.description: List, show, add, edit and delete the knowledge bases of a bot: the groups its articles are in, each with the language of its articles, the embedding profile the bot searches them with and how many results one search gives.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the knowledge bases of the bot (or --open the Knowledge bases screen in the web app).

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show one knowledge base with its revision (or --open the Knowledge bases screen in the web app).

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The knowledge base's id: camelCase, like offer. It does not change.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add a knowledge base to the bot.

options.name: --title
options.description: The title people see; unique within the bot, ignoring case and surrounding spaces.

options.name: --language
options.description: pl or en; the language of every article in the base. en when this is left out.

options.name: --embedding
options.description: The name of the embedding profile the bot embeds the base's articles with; the bot's environment holds its model. default when this is left out.

options.name: --results
options.description: How many results one search gives from the base, 1 to 20. 5 when this is left out.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The knowledge base's id: camelCase, like offer. It does not change.

commands.name: edit
commands.description: Change the title, the language, the embedding profile or the results per search of a knowledge base: only the options you give change. Its id stays, so whatever points at it still does.

options.name: --title
options.description: The new title.

options.name: --language
options.description: pl or en. Every article in the base takes it.

options.name: --embedding
options.description: The name of the embedding profile the bot embeds the base's articles with.

options.name: --results
options.description: How many results one search gives from the base, 1 to 20.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The knowledge base's id: camelCase, like offer. It does not change.

commands.name: delete
commands.description: Delete a knowledge base.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The knowledge base's id: camelCase, like offer. It does not change.

commands.name: procedures
commands.description: List, show, add, edit and delete the procedures of a bot.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the procedures of the bot, and what stops each from becoming a version (or --open the Procedures screen in the web app).

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show one procedure as YAML (or JSON with --json), both accepted back by `procedures edit --file`, or --open it in the web editor.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The procedure's id, like orderValuation.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add a procedure to the bot from a YAML or JSON file that holds the whole of it, and with --open show it in the web editor.

options.name: --file
options.description: A YAML or JSON file with the whole procedure: id, description, firstStep, steps, whenStalled, whenInterrupted, localFacts.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

commands.name: edit
commands.description: Replace a procedure with the whole of a YAML or JSON file (the output of `procedures show` is accepted back), and with --open show it in the web editor.

options.name: --file
options.description: A YAML or JSON file with the whole procedure: id, description, firstStep, steps, whenStalled, whenInterrupted, localFacts.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if the procedure is still at this revision (see `procedures show`); refused with the current revision otherwise. Default: the revision field of the file, else the latest.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The procedure's id, like orderValuation. It does not change.

commands.name: delete
commands.description: Delete a procedure. `conversation`, the base of every conversation, is always refused.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The procedure's id. `conversation` cannot be deleted.

commands.name: actions
commands.description: List, show, add, edit and delete the actions of a bot. A secret is written as {secret:NAME}, never as its value.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the actions of the bot, each with its implementation (or --open the Actions screen).

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show one action as YAML (or JSON with --json), both accepted back by `actions edit --file`, or --open it in the web.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The action's id, like checkServiceability.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add an action to the bot from a YAML or JSON file that holds the whole of it.

options.name: --file
options.description: A YAML or JSON file with the whole action: id, description, parameters, results, implementation.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

commands.name: edit
commands.description: Replace an action with the whole of a YAML or JSON file (the output of `actions show` is accepted back).

options.name: --file
options.description: A YAML or JSON file with the whole action: id, description, parameters, results, implementation.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The action's id. It does not change here: `suwagcms rename action` changes it.

commands.name: delete
commands.description: Delete an action that no procedure uses.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The action's id.

commands.name: test
commands.description: Try a saved action through the bot, which really calls the service, and show the results or the failure. Writes nothing (or --open its page, with the test panel, and call nothing).

options.name: --param
options.description: A parameter's value as name=value; repeat it for each parameter.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Really call the service: every method but GET, and every code action, asks for this first. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The action's id.

commands.name: persona
commands.description: Show and edit the persona of a bot: how it talks and what it talks about. It reaches the bot only with a version.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Print the persona as YAML, with its revision; `persona edit --file` takes this back with every text unchanged (or --open the Persona page in the web app).

commands.name: edit
commands.description: Replace the whole persona with a YAML or JSON file: what the file leaves out becomes empty. A YAML block such as `personality: |` keeps its line breaks.

options.name: --file
options.description: A YAML or JSON file with the whole persona: personality, and scope with inScope, outOfScope and whenOutOfScope.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if the persona is still at this revision (see `persona show`); refused with the current revision otherwise. Default: the revision field of the file, else the latest.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

commands.name: versions
commands.description: List the versions of a bot, create one from its working state, show one, or show what happened before it.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the versions of the bot, newest first (or --open the Versions screen in the web app).

commands.name: create
commands.description: Create a version from the bot's working state: refused with every mistake while the state is unfinished or has not changed since the latest version.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show one version with its document exactly as stored (or --open the version's page in the web app).

arguments.name: NUMBER
arguments.description: The version's number, like 14.

commands.name: window
commands.description: Show what happened from the previous version's creation through this version's, newest first (or --open the version's page).

options.name: --limit
options.description: How many entries a page holds, 50 unless said otherwise.

options.name: --before
options.description: Go on from this entry: the id the last page says.

options.name: --page
options.description: This numbered page, as the web counts them, with the total and each change written out.

arguments.name: NUMBER
arguments.description: The version's number, like 14.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Ask the bot which version it has (never what the CMS last sent), with the latest version, the versions still in use and the recent pushes (or --open the Versions screen in the web app).

commands.name: usage
commands.description: Show what uses a resource and what it uses, with the field of each reference (or --open its page, which lists them). Changes nothing.

arguments.name: KIND
arguments.description: fact, article, procedure or action.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The resource's id or, for a fact, its name.

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Change a resource's id and rewrite every reference to it, all or nothing; --dry-run lists what would be rewritten, --open opens the resource at its new address.

options.name: --if-revision
options.description: Apply only if it is still at this revision (see `show`); refused with the current revision otherwise.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: KIND
arguments.description: fact, kb, article, procedure or action.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The resource's id or, for a fact, its name.

arguments.name: NEWID
arguments.description: The id it gets, in the form that kind of resource requires.

commands.name: push
commands.description: Push the latest version, or the one --version names, to the bot and report the version the bot says it has; asks for no confirmation and sends nothing when it is already current.

options.name: --version
options.description: Push this kept version instead of the latest; that is the rollback, and it changes only the bot.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Say whether the version would be sent, made current or needs nothing, and what it changes; the bot stays as it is. [default: False]

commands.name: apply
commands.description: Apply a file of changes all or nothing: order inside it does not matter, and every mistake comes back at once.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --replace
options.description: An `add` of a resource the CMS already holds replaces the whole of it, as `edit --file` would; one that would store what is stored leaves it as it is, revision and history too. Nothing the file does not name is deleted. [default: False]

options.name: --compare
options.description: Say what applying the file with --replace would change, and change nothing: each change added, replaced with the fields and steps that differ, or unchanged, and what the CMS holds of the same kinds that the file does not name. Exit code 0 when nothing would change, 4 when something would, 1 when the file would be refused. [default: False]

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: A YAML or JSON file with a `changes` list of add, edit and delete.

commands.name: history
commands.description: Show what changed and when, newest first: every change to the bot, to one kind of resource, or to one resource, also after it is deleted (or --open the page).

options.name: --kind
options.description: Only the changes of this kind of resource, every one of it: fact, kb, article, procedure, action, persona or version.

options.name: --limit
options.description: How many entries a page holds, 50 unless said otherwise.

options.name: --before
options.description: Go on from this entry: the id the last page says.

options.name: --page
options.description: This numbered page, as the web counts them, with the total and each change written out.

arguments.name: KIND
arguments.description: fact, kb, article, procedure, action, persona or version. Left out with the id: every change to the bot.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The resource's id, a fact's name or a version's number; a persona, being one, has none.

commands.name: availability
commands.description: Turn articles, procedures and actions on and off, a live setting outside versions.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List every article, procedure and action, on or off, and say whether the bot has the setting. Changes nothing.

options.name: --stored
options.description: List what the CMS holds without asking the bot. [default: False]

commands.name: off
commands.description: Turn a resource off, at once and on every version; a resource in use needs --yes, and no reference breaks.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Turn it off although something uses it; the list is printed either way. [default: False]

arguments.name: KIND
arguments.description: article, procedure or action.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The resource's id.

commands.name: on
commands.description: Turn a resource on, at once and with no question.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Answer as the real command would, with the same refusals, and change nothing. [default: False]

arguments.name: KIND
arguments.description: article, procedure or action.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The resource's id.

commands.name: send
commands.description: Send everything that is off to the bot again, and exit 1 unless the bot confirms it.

commands.name: diff
commands.description: Say what going from one version to another changes: resources added, removed and changed, with old and new values. Finding differences exits 0 (or --open the comparison in the web app).

arguments.name: FROM
arguments.description: The version to compare from, like 12.

arguments.name: TO
arguments.description: The version to compare to, like 14.

commands.name: export
commands.description: Write a version to a folder of YAML files for reading and searching; changes to those files do nothing (or --open the version in the web app).

options.name: --out
options.description: A new or empty folder to write the files to.

arguments.name: NUMBER
arguments.description: The version's number, like 14; the latest when left out.

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Check a definition with the validator of the CMS, for a bot outside .NET: it stores nothing and contacts no bot. Exit code 0 for no mistakes, 1 otherwise.

options.name: --file
options.description: A YAML or JSON file with a whole definition.

options.name: --declaration
options.description: A YAML or JSON file with what a bot declares: also report what that bot cannot run.

options.name: --stage
options.description: The stage to check at. [default: version]
